full_judgment:
Md. Kamrul Hossain Mollah, J: By this Rule, the accused petitioner by filing an application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (briefly as the Code) sought for quashing of the proceeding of CR Case No. 6235 of 2010 under section 406/420 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Pending hearing of the Rule issuing order dated 18-6-2012 let all further proceeding of the CR Case No. 6235 of 2010 under section 406/420 of the Penal Code now pending in the Court of learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka be stayed for a period of 6 (six) months from date and subsequently stay granted earlier by the Court be extended from time to time. 

 3. The relevant facts, for the purpose of disposal of this rule, are that one Md Liakat Ali, Proprietor, SA Enterprise, 87 Purana Paltan Line, Paltan Tower, Suit No. 605 PS-Paltan, Dhaka as a complainant filed a petition of complaint on 23-11-2010 against the present petitioner mentioning occurrences dated 8-11-2009, 9-2-2010, 2-11-2010 and 15-11-2010 before the Chief Metro-politan Magistrate, Dhaka under section 406/420 of the Penal Code, alleging inter alia, that the parties maintained business on credit and on 11-8-2009 against the chemical equipment for business purpose a cheque of Taka 5,50.000 was given to the opposite party No. 2, when the cheque was placed before the bank on 9-2-2010 the cheque was dishonoured by the bank for insufficiency of fund. The petitioner demanded the cheque amount of money repeatedly to the accused petitioner but the accused petitioner did not pay the cheque amount within time and very carefully and intentionally gave hope to pay the cheque amount and passed the stipulated period negligently. Lastly, on 15-11-2010 on demand of the money by the complainant, the accused petitioner denied to pay the cheque amount to him and that is why the instant case was lodged under section 406/420 of the Penal Code. 

 5. The case has been transferred to the 'Court of Mr. AGM Al Masud, learned Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka who after hearing framed charge against the petitioner by order dated 26-8-2010. 

 6. Feeling aggrieved the accused-petitioner has come to this Court .under section 561A of the code of Criminal Procedure challenging the proceeding of the above CR case and obtained the present Rule and stay order. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr. Md. Ruhul Amin Shikder, the learned Advocate on behalf of the complainant opposite party no. 2 and the learned Deputy Attorney-General along with learned Assistant Attorney-General appearing for the state opposite party no. 1 oppose the Rule and their common intention that trial court after Considering the materials on record rightly framed the charge under section 406/420 of the Penal Code against the accused petitioner. There is a initial deception in this case and prima facie case has been made out in the petition of complaint which calls for no interference by this court. 

 10. On going to the materials on record it transpires that the complainant in its petition of complaint categorically narrated the manner of crime committed by the accused petitioner. Admittedly, the accused-petitioner maintained business with Opposite Party No. 2 on credit and on 11-8-2009 against the chemical equipment for business purpose a cheque of Taka 5,50,000 was given to the opposite party No. 2. When the cheque was placed before the bank on 9-2-2010 the cheque was dishonored by the bank for insufficiency of fund. More so, in the complaint it was asserted that the petitioner demanded the cheque amount of money repeatedly to the accused petitioner but the accused petitioner did not pay the cheque amount within time and very Carefully and intentionally gave hope to pay the cheque amount and passed the stipulated period negligently. With this regard reliance has been placed in the case of Abdul. Rahim alias ANM Abdur Rahman vs Enamul Haq and another 43 DLR (AD) 173. All that is required at the stage of framing charge is to see whether the prima-facie case regarding commission of certain offence is made out. The truth veracity and effect of evidence which prosecution proposes to adduce at the time is not to be meticulously judged at the stage of framing charge. In the instant case the accused stand indicted for offence punishable under section 406/420 of the Penal Code. Cognizance has been taken under the said section. We have meticulously examined the allegations made by the complainant and we find that the offence punishable under aforesaid section of the Penal Code have been clearly disclosed in the instant case against the accused. We have gone through the grounds taken in the Miscellaneous case and we find that such grounds are absolutely the disputed question of facts and the same should be decided at trial. The pleas of the petitioner are nothing but the defence plea. Be that as it may the proposition of law is now well settled that on the basis of defence plea or materials the criminal proceedings should not be stifled before trial; when there is a prima-facie case for going for trial. In view of such facts the grounds taken in the petition of Misc case are not the correct exposition of law. More so interruption of the course of Justice will set up a wrong precedent by which the course of justice instead of being advanced readily been stifled inasmuch as the grounds advanced before us are not correct or legal exposition of law. Therefore we hold that there are sufficient grounds for proceeding against the accused for going for trial under section 406/420 of the Penal Code. To that end in view we are at one with the learned Judge of the Court below regarding framing of charge against the accused. In view of the above we failed to discover any merit in this Rule. Thus the Rule having no merit fails. 

 13. In view of the facts, this is a case of 2010, we are inclined to direct the Court below to dispose of the case as early as possible preferably Within 3 (three) months from failing of any installment mentioned above.
